mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate directly lowers discount rates for equity valuation models, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as capital costs decrease.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS declines but S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in >55% of instances, or Rank IC < 0.02 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A 0.2pp monthly unemployment rate increase signals labor market deterioration, reducing consumer spending power and triggering negative S&P 500 returns within 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in >55% of UNRATE >0.2pp monthly rise instances, or signal Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent growth in housing starts and retail sales indicates robust consumer demand, accelerating corporate earnings growth and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Joint HOUST/RSAFS growth fails to produce positive 20-day returns in >55% of cases, or interaction term p-value >0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production during supply chain disruption regimes creates stagflationary pressures, forcing aggressive monetary tightening that causes negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: In INDPRO decline regimes, S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in >55% of cases, or regime-specific Rank IC < 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: Federal funds rate exceeding 5.0% signals restrictive monetary policy that suppresses corporate investment, leading to negative S&P 500 returns within 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in >55% of FEDFUNDS >5.0% instances, or signal Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Strong nonfarm payrolls growth directly correlates with rising consumer spending, boosting corporate revenue visibility and generating positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Positive PAYEMS growth fails to produce positive 5-day returns in >55% of cases, or signal Rank IC < 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: Accelerating real GDP growth above 2.0% quarterly signals robust economic expansion, driving corporate earnings momentum and positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: In GDPC1 >2.0% growth regimes, S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in >55% of cases, or regime-specific Rank IC < 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous industrial production decline and CPI inflation surge indicates stagflation, triggering central bank rate hikes that cause negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: Joint INDPRO decline/CPIAUCSL rise fails to produce negative 20-day returns in >55% of cases, or interaction term p-value >0.05.
